relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: Intravenous infusion of CGRP caused a delayed migraine-like headache in about 63% of migraine patients (50–77%)

relationships.subject: PACAP
relationships.evidence_quote: intravenous infusion of PACAP-38 caused a delayed migraine-like headache in about 68% of migraine patients (58–73%)

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: Central (intracerebroventricular, thalamic, and cerebellar) and peripheral (intraperitoneal) injection of CGRP induced light aversion in wildtype mice

relationships.subject: PACAP
relationships.evidence_quote: intraperitoneal injection of PACAP caused light aversion coupled with increased resting in the dark and no anxiety in the open field

relationships.subject: Anti-CGRP antibody
relationships.evidence_quote: CGRP-induced responses could be blocked by an anti-CGRP antibody, but not by an anti-PACAP antibody

relationships.subject: Anti-PACAP antibody
relationships.evidence_quote: PACAP-induced responses could be blocked with a monoclonal anti-PACAP antibody, but not by an anti-CGRP antibody

relationships.subject: PACAP
relationships.evidence_quote: PACAP can induce release of CGRP from rat trigeminal neurons

key_findings: CGRP and PACAP infusions induce migraine-like attacks in about two-thirds of patients, but only PACAP causes premonitory-like symptoms.
In mice CGRP and PACAP cause light aversion via independent mechanisms; antibodies against one do not block the other.
